scope: Complete author reading of the public quickstart, all fourteen Getting Started pages and all ten tutorial pages, reconciled with the existing installed-wheel, PostgreSQL, REST, task, Durable Operation, MCP, scaffold and operator evidence. This is a semantic and usability review, not an independent novice study or a final-candidate rerun.

reviews.reason: Routes an evaluator to the exact first-project journey, preserves PostgreSQL and identity prerequisites, and defers MCP, tenancy and AI until after the first protected REST application.
Provides one ordered beginner route and separates optional advanced and experimental paths.
Distinguishes distribution and import names, public-wheel and source installs, PostgreSQL ownership, generated-project packaging limits and environment verification.
Keeps the first ten minutes to project creation and points to the exact files and executable checks instead of duplicating an incomplete mini-application.
Gives one coherent model, migration, protected REST, local identity and test sequence whose installed-wheel PostgreSQL execution is separately recorded.
Directs legacy entry traffic to the canonical application and explains the model, ViewSet, migration and authentication sequence without another divergent example.
Matches the basic scaffold tree, startapp output, installed-app and route responsibilities, and distinguishes the flat domain templates.
Uses the global settings object and explicit constructor handoff, states precedence and reload limits, and delegates the full contract to one reference.
Separates local dbsetup from production role provisioning, gives a bounded pool probe, and explains URL precedence, lifecycle and role/RLS limits.
Distinguishes dev and production startup, health and readiness, MCP and inspection URLs, process-local services and graceful shutdown.
Classifies all repository examples by teaching purpose and defects, and separates structural validation from authenticated execution.
Explains the basic versus flat domain-template shapes and directs tenant users away from the defective historical multitenant example.
Starts from server-owned machine identity and explicit exposure, uses the official synchronous transport, and denies protocol Tasks or implied durability.
Keeps provider execution experimental, uses real AI Hub commands and environment names, and now anchors exclusions to the released v0.7 contract.
Keeps Studio disabled by default, gives a loopback-only unauthenticated development profile and names the stronger production prerequisites.
Lists the six sequential Ticket Desk stages and separates supplementary patterns and production how-to material.
Adds one nullable relation, serializer validation and a reviewed additive migration while preserving authentication and explicit non-tenant scope.
Combines trusted membership, application permission, relation ownership and forced RLS under a restricted role, with explicit production backfill limits.
Uses a read-only tenant report to teach persisted tasks while disclosing the missing full Principal reauthorization and unfenced recovery boundary.
Covers registration, admission, one-shot workers, bounded idempotency, retry rollback, cancellation and current role resolution in the supported postgres_atomic boundary.
Uses the official client and server-owned MCP AgentPrincipal to prove shared CRUD validation and denial while keeping durable human dispatch separate.
Replaces the incomplete historical tutorial with links to the canonical implementation and accurately limits the supplementary Blog example.
Explains the complete isolation stack and directs users to the tested Ticket Desk path instead of the defective historical template.
Keeps synchronous MCP as the stable agent access path, marks query and provider helpers experimental, and now anchors exclusions to v0.7.
Orders configuration, migration roles, RLS, Doctor, workers, retention and upgrade responsibilities and preserves operator-owned infrastructure boundaries.

contradictions.boundary: Two experimental AI entry pages still described exclusions relative to the superseded v0.6 contract after v0.7.0 was released.
contradictions.disposition: Both pages now anchor experimental exclusions to the stable v0.7 contract.
